thread:
incident-bot: Paging @sara (oncall) — High-severity alert: ZettaCorp private VPC (dedicated pool) showing NLB 5xx healthcheck failures across us-west-2a/b. Route53 records still resolving but 30% of connections failing. Alert: nlb-health-err > 5m

sara (oncall): I’m on it. Acknowledge and joining. Can someone confirm customer impact?

jon (cust-succ): Zetta reporting 503s for API->inference route. They say ~20% of requests time out or 503 over the last 10 minutes. High priority for them.

alisa (eng-sre): Adding context: Dedicated pool for Zetta is on private VPC with NLB in front of model nodes. Recent security-groups change by infra earlier today rolled out to that VPC (ticket INF-6123). Suspecting SG or NLB healthcheck source IPs blocked.

mike (netops): I can pull NLB flow logs. Quick check: NLB healthchecks hitting instances but backend reset with RST from instance side. Also seeing TCP RST from 10.0.12.45 (sg-zetta-app) to healthcheck IPs.

irfan (infra): I rolled the SG change. It was intended to tighten outbound to specific prefixes. I’ll review. If we need an emergency rollback I can revert.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-zetta-vpc-nlb. Severity: P1. Oncall: sara. Runbook: private-vpc-nlb-failure-v1. Link: https://redwood.runbooks/INC-20260315-zetta-vpc-nlb

sara (oncall): Step 1: validate healthchecks failing: alisa please paste recent /var/log/nginx or app logs from a node so we can see healthcheck responses.

alisa (eng-sre): Pasting trimmed logs: 
```
[03-15T15:00:12Z] GET /health -> 200 ms
[03-15T15:01:01Z] GET /health -> 200 ms
[03-15T15:07:34Z] GET /health -> connection reset by peer
[03-15T15:07:34Z] ERROR: read tcp 10.0.12.45:80->10.10.10.5:55012: read: connection reset by peer
```
Looks like resets started ~15:07 UTC correlating with SG deploy at 15:05.

mike (netops): Confirmed. Flow log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T15:07:34Z ACCEPT tcp 10.10.10.5:55012 -> 10.0.12.45:80 0x0
2026-03-15T15:07:34Z REJECT tcp 10.0.12.45:80 -> 10.10.10.5:55012 RST
```
Healthcheck IPs are from the NLB. Looks like outbound allowed list blocked the return traffic.

irfan (infra): Okay that matches: my SG change replaced a broad outbound allow 0.0.0.0/0 with a narrower set (internal prefixes + customer CIDRs). I’ll revert the SG for the Zetta app subnet to the previous rule set immediately. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: SG-change rollback started by irfan. Change-id: ch-87912. Estimated time to converge: 60s per AZ.

mike (netops): While we wait, add mitigation: temporarily allow NLB healthcheck CIDR ranges in the security group outbound. Command I ran in customer lab: 
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-zetta-app --protocol tcp --port 80 --cidr 10.10.10.0/24
```
But better to revert infra change as planned.

jon (cust-succ): Let Zetta know we have identified probable cause (SG outbound restricting NLB responses) and are rolling a rollback/mitigation. They want timeframe.

sara (oncall): ETA from infra?

irfan (infra): Rollback complete for us-west-2a/b. Verified rules: outbound 0.0.0.0/0 again present for app sg.

mike (netops): Re-checking flow logs and ALBs: healthchecks now succeed, backend connections established. Quick smoke: curl to NLB DNS forwarded fine from our test host.

alisa (eng-sre): App logs showing healthchecks resumed: 
```
[03-15T15:09:47Z] GET /health -> 200 ms
[03-15T15:10:02Z] GET /health -> 200 ms
```

jon (cust-succ): Zetta reports drop to <1% error rate now. They say they saw a brief spike ~15:07-15:09. Thanking team.

sara (oncall): Good. Root cause hypothesis: recent SG tightening removed outbound allow to NLB healthcheck source IPs, causing RSTs. Immediate mitigation: rollback done. Next steps: create targeted permanent rule and tighten least-privilege without breaking healthchecks.

alisa (eng-sre): Recommend permanent fix: add explicit allow for NLB healthcheck CIDRs + route for cross-AZ traffic. Also add a pre-deploy check in INF change workflow to run healthcheck-only dry-run against dedicated pools.

irfan (infra): I’ll open INF-6180 to: (1) add explicit inbound/outbound rules for healthcheck CIDRs, (2) rework change pipeline to include automated connectivity tests to customer VPCs, (3) add rollout canary to one AZ first.

mike (netops): Also lower Route53 TTL for the affected record to 30s during the change window next time, and prepare ALB fallback plan in runbook.

incident-bot: Update INC-20260315-zetta-vpc-nlb: mitigation applied, incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Paging cleared for oncall after confirmation.

sara (oncall): Monitor for 30m then we can close if stable. Alisa, can you collect logs and save to incident folder for postmortem?

alisa (eng-sre): On it — saving logs and timeline to /incidents/INC-20260315-zetta-vpc-nlb/artifacts.

jon (cust-succ): I’ll follow up with Zetta with a brief incident summary and next steps.

sara (oncall): Thanks everyone. Postmortem owner: irfan. Please include action items: add healthcheck rules, change pipeline test, and a runbook update. Closing timeline in 30m if no regression. :white_check_mark:
